subject: Modeling help - How to fit spline model for a parameter?

messages.author: ba47d4626a81b156
messages.subject: Modeling help - How to fit spline model for a parameter?
parts:
Dear Stan users, 

I want to fit a spline model for log(theta). As shown below.


I wanted to write spline (log(theta)) as  X[i] * beta + Z[i] * b, where  X = cbind(1, log(theta)), Z = outer(log(theta), knots, "-")*(outer(log(theta), knots, "-")>0). 

Knots are defined in R script. But I don't know how to define X and Z in stan. There is no matches for function name="outer" in stan, and I can't create a dummy variable by (outer(log(theta), knots, "-")>0). 

The stan code I tried is: 

data {
    int<lower=0> n;          // number of subjects
    int<lower=0> K;          // number of knots
    int<lower=0> P;       
    real<lower=0> knots[]   
    real<lower=0> BP[n];    
    real<lower=0> logVarSE[n];    //log(estimated SE^2)
}

parameters {
  real<lower=0> mu;
  real<lower=0> sigmabeta;
  real<lower=0> tau1;
  real<lower=0> tau2;
  vector<lower=0>[n] theta;
  vector<lower=0>[n] sigmaepsilon2;   //sigmaepsilon square
  vector[p] beta;
  vector[K] b;
}

model {
        row_vector[P] X[n];
        X<- append_col(1, theta);
        row_vector[K] z[n];
        z<-outer(log(theta),knots)*(outer(log(theta), knots)>0);

        for (j in 1:n){
        BP[j] ~ normal(theta[j], sqrt(sigmaepsilon2[j]));
        theta[j] ~ normal(mu,sigmabeta);
        sigmaepsilon2[j] ~ lognormal(X[j] * beta + Z[j] * b,tau1);
        logVarSE[j] ~ normal(log(sigmaepsilon2[j]),tau2);
    }
 }

I also attach my data and r script. 

Thank you very much. 

Chubing
